In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. My true minimum is 0.1155. If others are genuinely bidding at their cost floors (F1: 0.1192, F2: 0.1447, F4: 0.1155, F5: 0.1211), and F0 is being "conservative" (likely slightly above their 0.1117 from last round, maybe 0.1150-0.1175), and F3 says "responsibly from cost floor" but had the lowest bid last round...

I should bid exactly at my cost floor - 0.1155. If I win, the second price will be paid by whoever bid second lowest. If others genuinely bid at their stated floors, the clearing price would be around 0.1155-0.1192 range, which would be profitable for me.
